citationAllowlist.reason: Named once in SKILL.md, in the list of things this skill deliberately does NOT do — ISO 27001 and CIS identifiers are excluded from the requirement view. Naming a standard in order to say it is out of scope makes no claim about its text, its numbering or its requirements, and a verified row would assert a reading nobody performed. CAC also holds no ISO licence, so no ISO/IEC text can be read or reproduced here. Permanent, not pending: the same constraint recorded on the nist-csf and vendor-register rows.

sources.label: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
sources.instrument: NIST CSWP 29, GV.PO-01 and GV.PO-02 with their implementation examples, and ID.IM-04
sources.howChecked: Read against the bundled CPRT export rather than from recall: skills/nist-csf/references/nist-csf-2.0-core.json, whose own provenance records csf-2.0.xlsx sha256 cc4ec545...f9b616. GV.PO-01 carries 5 implementation examples and GV.PO-02 carries 4; every example quoted in references/policy.md is verbatim from that file. The claim that the CSF Core itself maps GV.PO-01/-02 onto all twenty SP 800-53 '-1' controls was verified the same way, in the subcategories' informativeReferences (AC-01 through SR-01, listed for both Rev 5.1.1 and Rev 5.2.0). ID.IM-04's wording was read from the same file.

sources.label: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5
sources.instrument: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, the Policy and Procedures ('-1') control in each control family
sources.howChecked: The twenty control ids and their family labels were not typed. They were generated from the bundled crosswalk skills/nist-csf/references/crosswalks/800-53-r5.catalog.json — 206 controls, exactly 20 matching ^[A-Z]{2}-1$ — and evals/requirement-drift.sh regenerates the vendored copy from that same file on every run and compares all 112 fields. Control titles are the crosswalk's verbatim public-domain labels; no control text is reproduced, and the crosswalk carries none (every `text` is null).
